Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Butylated hydroxyanisole, usually abbreviated BHA, is a mixture of two isomers of a phenolic antioxidant. Its antioxidant role is to slow oxidation that can cause rancidity or unwanted colour changes during storage. The specified material is supplied as white flakes or waxy solid. The specification describes it as effectively insoluble in water.
more_info.side_effects:
Refined food-use estimates were generally below EFSA's limit.
High-dose animal studies reported effects on offspring growth and survival; rodent forestomach findings have uncertain human relevance.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain sweet baked goods; sauces; potato-, cereal-, flour- or starch-based snacks; processed nuts; nut butters and nut spreads; non-heat–treated meat products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
